alice: Quick check — if we keep a 25% safety margin on top of modeled peak, how long can we run primarily on preemptible GPUs before SLAs risk? seeing a steady evening uptick in EU tokens/sec this week. cc @ben_infra @dan_sre

ben_infra: Short answer: depends on eviction pattern. I ran the headroom sim this morning. With current peak=1.2M tokens/s EU evening, preemptible pool 160 GPUs, avg gpu sustained ~7.5k tokens/s => raw capacity ~1.2M tokens/s (160*7.5k). With 25% margin we need ~1.5M tokens/s -> ~200 GPUs. So shortfall ~40 GPUs.

dan_sre: Exact — and note preemptible churn adds variance. If we model a 10% sudden eviction within 60s, that eats most of margin. We should plan for either 40 reserved GPUs or cross-region spill to US-west as fast fallback.

carol_prod: Are we seeing any request QoS degradation now? on the canary dashboards yesterday I noticed tail latencies creeping after 21:00 CET but not full failures.

ben_infra: tail latency bump corresponds to prefix-cache miss rate increase and CPU queueing on hosts that are close to burst concurrency. No 5xx spike yet. Suggest ephemeral warmup threads and stricter per-route concurrency caps.

emily_fin: Cost perspective — 40 reserved GPUs (p3-equivalent) monthly vs relying on preemptibles + on-demand fallback: reserving saves ~22% on average but costs baseline even in low season. If traffic grows 15% YoY, reserved looks better after ~7 months.

alice: Can we get concrete numbers — tell me monthly GPU-hours gap and expected egress/network constraints if we shift 10% load to us-west fallback during evenings.

ben_infra: Paste of the quick calc I ran: ```
# assumptions
peak_tokens_sec = 1_200_000
safety_margin = 0.25
gpu_tokens_sec = 7500   # conservative sustained
preemptible_gpus = 160
reserved_needed = ceil((peak_tokens_sec*(1+safety_margin))/gpu_tokens_sec)
# evaluate
reserved_needed  # => 200 GPUs
reserve_gap = reserved_needed - preemptible_gpus  # => 40 GPUs
monthly_gpu_hours_gap = reserve_gap * 24 * 30  # => 40*720 = 28800 GPU-hours
```

ben_infra: Network note: shifting 10% of EU evening traffic to us-west adds ~120k tokens/sec cross-region egress. That's ~15TB/day outbound if avg token payloads + overhead ~125 bytes/token (very rough). We hit egress caps and cost centers quickly. Also increases latency for EU users — fallback only for non-latency-sensitive routes.

dan_sre: Operational risk matrix: 1) Reserve 40 GPUs in eu-west — low latency, costs baseline, reduces eviction risk. 2) Keep preemptible + fast fallback — cheaper, higher operational complexity and egress cost, potential SLA blips. 3) Hybrid: reserve 20 GPUs + fallback 10% spill — good compromise. Recommend experiment hybrid for 60 days with traffic shaping.

carol_prod: 👍 Hybrid sounds sensible. For canaries we can mark low-QoS routes to spill first; will add tags to routing rules.

emily_fin: I'll run the finance sensitivity for three scenarios (reserve40, reserve20+spill, pure preemptible+fallback) and include egress cost buckets. ETA EOD tomorrow.

alice: Great. Action items: ben to schedule hybrid canary and add per-route caps (ben noted), dan to add runbook for cross-region spill and SLA thresholds, emily to share cost sensitivity. We’ll reconvene after finance numbers. :thumbsup:

ben_infra: On it. I'll post the canary schedule and flags here when ready.

dan_sre: I'll draft the spill runbook and rollback playbook today.

emily_fin: Will post numbers by EOD tomorrow.
